title: Maximum Ascending Subarray Sum
statement: You get an array `nums` of positive integers. Look at every contiguous stretch of `nums` (a subarray) whose elements keep getting strictly bigger from left to right; a single element counts as such a stretch. Return the largest total that any of these stretches adds up to.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every subarray and testing whether it ascends works for 100 numbers, but there is a simpler view: the array splits into maximal ascending runs, and each run ends exactly where the next one starts. Inside a run the sum only grows (all values are positive), so the best sum of any run is its full total. One left-to-right pass that keeps a running total of the current run finds every run total.

## Approach

1. Start both `best` and `current` at `nums[0]`: the first element is a run of length one.
2. For each index `i` from 1, compare `nums[i]` with `nums[i - 1]`.
3. If it is strictly bigger, the run continues: add `nums[i]` to `current`.
4. Otherwise a new run starts at `i`: reset `current` to `nums[i]`.
5. After each step, keep the larger of `best` and `current`, then return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [10, 20, 30, 5, 10, 50]`. Start with `current = best = 10`. Then 20 and 30 extend the run: `current` becomes 30 and 60, so `best = 60`. At 5 the run breaks and `current = 5`. Then 10 and 50 extend it: `current` becomes 15 and 65, and `best` rises to 65, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each element is looked at once.
- Space: O(1): only two running totals.

## Pitfalls

- The comparison must be strict: equal neighbours such as `[3, 3]` break the run.
- Update `best` after every element, not only when a run ends, or the last run is missed.
- A single element is a valid run, so the answer is never smaller than the largest value.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | largest run total seen so far |
| `current` | total of the ascending run ending at `i` |
| `i` | index of the element being added |

narration.2: The first element alone is a run, so it is the best total so far.
narration.3: The current run also starts with just the first element.
narration.5: Walk through the rest of the array one element at a time.
narration.6: Is this element strictly bigger than the one before it?
narration.7: Yes: the ascending run continues, so add the element to its total.
narration.9: No: a new run starts here with only this element.
narration.11: Keep the largest run total seen so far.
narration.13: Every run has been totalled; return the biggest one.
